# Zephyrium Docs

> Documentation for Zephyrium, a privacy-preserving layer-1 chain with the ZEP coin.

This file contains all documentation content in a single document following the llmstxt.org standard.

## Concepts

Zephyrium is a layer-1 chain where privacy is the default for transfers.

### What is private

| | Transfers of ZEP and tokens | Swaps on pDEX | Staking |
|---|---|---|---|
| Sender | Hidden in a ring of 8 | Hidden in a ring of 8 | Public |
| Receiver | One-time address | One-time address | Public |
| Amount | Hidden | **Public** | Public |
| Which token | Hidden for tokens in confidential-asset mode | **Public** | ZEP only |

Three mechanisms do the work:

- **Ring signatures.** A spend is signed by a ring of eight keys. One is the real spender; seven are decoys taken from the chain.
- **One-time addresses.** Every payment lands on a fresh address derived for that payment, so two payments to the same person look unrelated.
- **Hidden amounts.** Amounts are commitments. A range proof shows the amount is valid and that inputs equal outputs, without revealing the number.

### How the chain is built

- **Shards** process transactions, token transfers and swaps. The devnet runs one shard.
- **The beacon chain** coordinates the shards: it records who the validators are, confirms shard blocks and carries messages between shards.
- **Committees** of validators sign blocks. A block is final when more than two thirds of the committee sign it.
- **The highway** is a relay that every node connects to. It introduces nodes to each other and forwards their messages.

[Node types](/validators/node-types) explains who runs each part.

### Current limits

These are known and on the [roadmap](/resources/roadmap):

- **Small rings with uniform decoys.** Eight members, chosen without regard to coin age, is weaker than a larger, age-aware ring.
- **Swap amounts are public.** pDEX hides who trades, not how much or which pair.
- **The highway is a single relay.** It can see which address a transaction came from, and the chain stops if it is down.
- **Fixed committee seats.** On the devnet, 5 of 7 shard seats and all 4 beacon seats are held by fixed validators.
- **Wallets share a viewing key with their node.** A wallet registers a viewing key with the node it uses so the node can find its coins.
- **No slashing penalty.** A validator that misbehaves loses its seat and gets its stake back.

---

## Quick start

A devnet is a complete private network on one machine: a highway, 4 beacon validators, 5 shard validators and a full node. It produces a block about every 10 seconds.

### Requirements

- Go 1.24 or newer, python3, curl
- macOS or Linux. Only macOS on Apple Silicon has been tested.
- Free ports: 9330, 9334-9344, 9350-9354, 9434-9454

### 1. Create the keys (once)

Validator and treasury keys live in `secrets/secrets.json`, which is git-ignored. On a new machine:

```bash
mkdir -p secrets && cd secrets
GO111MODULE=on GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go run -ldflags=-checklinkname=0 ../utility/genzephyriumkeys
# writes keylist.json, keylist-v2.json and secrets.json into this folder
cp keylist.json keylist-v2.json ../config/local/
cd ..
GO111MODULE=on GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go run -ldflags=-checklinkname=0 ./utility/gengenesis
```

`gengenesis` adds a foundation key to `secrets/secrets.json`, writes the genesis allocation to `config/local/init_tx.json`, and sets `dao_address` in `config/local/param.yaml` to the foundation address. Nothing to paste by hand.

Back up `secrets/secrets.json`. It is the only copy of the private keys.

### 2. Build

```bash
GO111MODULE=on GOFLAGS=-mod=mod go build -ldflags=-checklinkname=0 -o incognito ./
```

The `-ldflags=-checklinkname=0` flag is required with Go 1.24 or newer.

### 3. Launch

```bash
./launch_local.sh
```

This builds the highway on first use, starts it, then starts the nodes one second apart. Logs go to `logs/`, chain data to `data/`.

### 4. Check

```bash
python3 tests/devnet/check.py
```

It checks block production, the genesis balance, the stake rules, the reward split after the first epoch, and a DEX swap. It takes about 10 minutes because it waits for an epoch to end. Add `--stakers` to also stake two outside validators and wait until one is seated and paid (about 30 minutes; start `./start_node.sh shard0-5` and `./start_node.sh shard0-6` first).

To query the chain yourself, the full node answers JSON-RPC on port 9354:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://127.0.0.1:9354 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"jsonrpc":"1.0","method":"getblockchaininfo","params":[],"id":1}'
```

### 5. Stop and reset

```bash
./stop_local.sh          # stops only this folder's nodes and highway
rm -rf data logs         # optional: the next launch starts a new chain at block 1
```

A reset is required after changing genesis or committee settings. Do not use the inherited `stop.sh`; it closes every tmux session on the machine.

### Nodes and ports

| Node | Role | Peer port | RPC port |
|---|---|---|---|
| highway | Introduces nodes and relays messages | 9330 | none |
| beacon-0 to beacon-3 | Beacon validators | 9450-9453 | 9350-9353 |
| shard0-0 to shard0-3 | Fixed shard validators | 9434-9437 | 9334-9337 |
| shard0-4 | Fixed shard validator | 9442 | 9342 |
| shard0-5, shard0-6 | Spare nodes for staked validators | 9443, 9444 | 9343, 9344 |
| full_node | Follows all chains; query this one | 9454 | 9354 |

## ZEP Documentation

import {Hero, QuickStart, CardGrid, Card, UseCases, Pills, Status, CTA} from '@site/src/components/Home';

Run a node, stake as a validator and build on a privacy chain that hides who paid whom and how much.

### Guides

  A full private network on one machine
  Stake, get a seat, earn rewards
  One billion cap, released over 21 years
  Trade in pools built into the chain

### Use cases

### Products

  Browser wallet; keys stay on your device
  Pools and swaps built into the chain
  Private tokens anyone can create
  What is private, and how the chain is built

### Network status

  There is no public testnet or mainnet yet. Everything in these docs runs on a devnet you start yourself.

### Resources

  One script starts a highway, four beacon validators, five shard validators and a full node on your machine.

---

## pDEX

pDEX is an exchange that is part of the chain itself: pools and swaps are handled by the validators, with no separate contract to deploy.

### How it works

- **Pools** hold two assets and price swaps with the constant-product rule: the product of the two balances stays the same through a trade.
- **Liquidity providers** add both assets to a pool. A position is tied to a position key that the provider mints once.
- **Swaps** burn the asset being sold and pay out the asset being bought to a one-time address.

| Setting | Devnet value |
|---|---|
| Default pool fee | 0.30% |
| Highest fee a pool can have | 2% |
| Cost to mint a position key | 1 ZEP |

### What is private, and what is not

| | On pDEX today |
|---|---|
| Who traded | Hidden: the trade is signed by a ring of 8 |
| Where the proceeds go | Hidden: a one-time address |
| Amount sold | **Public** |
| Token pair | **Public** |

pDEX gives anonymous trades, not confidential ones. Hiding swap amounts is a research item on the [roadmap](/resources/roadmap).

### Try it on the devnet

The devnet check creates a test token, adds a ZEP pool for it and swaps 1 ZEP:

```bash
python3 tests/devnet/check.py
```

The last line of its output reports the swap, for example `DEX swap: 1 ZEP bought 1.998002 pUSDt`.

### Names in the code

The RPC methods carry the same name in lowercase: `pdexv3_getState`, `pdexv3_txAddLiquidity` and `pdexv3_txTrade`.

### Known limit

A single admin key can still change pDEX parameters such as fee rates. Removing it is the first phase of the [roadmap](/resources/roadmap).

---

## pTokens

An pToken is a token on Zephyrium that moves with the same privacy as ZEP: the sender hides in a ring, the receiver gets a one-time address and the amount is hidden.

### Creating one

Any account can create a token with a fixed supply in one transaction. The whole supply is issued to the creator.

On the devnet this is the `createandsendtokeninittransaction` RPC method, and pWallet lists the new token once it arrives. A newly created token needs a few blocks before it can be spent.

### Privacy of a token transfer

| | Visible to the public? |
|---|---|
| Sender | No |
| Receiver | No |
| Amount | No |
| Which token | Hidden for tokens in confidential-asset mode; visible otherwise |

Making confidential-asset mode the rule for every token is on the [roadmap](/resources/roadmap).

### What is planned

- **Issuer-owned tokens** with a public registry entry and an optional mintable supply.
- **An auditor key per token**, so an issuer can show activity to a regulator without showing it to everyone.
- **Private distributions** such as dividends to current holders.

### Known limit

The code inherited a central issuing key that can mint new tokens. It is scheduled for removal in the first phase of the [roadmap](/resources/roadmap).

---

## pWallet

pWallet is a Chrome extension wallet for the Zephyrium devnet. It builds private transactions in the browser, so spending keys never leave your device.

:::note Devnet only
pWallet is not in the Chrome Web Store. It is loaded as an unpacked extension and connects to a devnet node. Coins on a devnet have no value.
:::

### What it does

| Feature | Details |
|---|---|
| Send and receive ZEP | Payments land on one-time addresses automatically |
| Tokens | Lists every pToken you hold and sends them |
| pDEX | Add liquidity and swap from the popup |
| Connect to apps | Web pages can request a connection, balances and transactions; each needs your approval |

### How it protects keys

- The wallet seed is encrypted on your device with your password.
- Ring signatures and range proofs are computed in the browser, then the finished transaction is sent to a node.
- Building a transaction takes roughly 5 to 15 seconds, and the popup has to stay open while it does.

### What the node learns

To find your coins, the wallet registers a **viewing key** with the node it uses. That node can see your incoming coins; it cannot spend them. Use a node you run yourself if that matters to you. Removing this step is on the [roadmap](/resources/roadmap).

### Fees on the devnet

| Transaction | Minimum fee |
|---|---|
| ZEP transfer | 0.1 ZEP |
| Token transaction | 10 ZEP |

---

## Changelog

Changes to the Zephyrium chain. Newest first.

### 2026-11-02

- Tokenomics v4, the three pillars: every block reward is split in three equal parts, 323/969 each to validators, liquidity providers and the DAO treasury. The liquidity part is minted on-chain at the end of each epoch into the pDEX (SWAP) pools, weighted by each pool's ZEP reserve unless governance sets per-pool weights; providers withdraw it with their LP fees. While no pool holds ZEP that part goes to the DAO treasury.
- ICO reduced to 31,000,000 ZEP pre-minted at genesis; blocks mint 969,000,000 ZEP (`basic_reward` 34.478342477 ZEP, `max_reward` 969M). The wallet behind `dao_address` is now the DAO treasury.
- `check.py` verifies the split before and after a pool exists. Consensus change: the project devnet needs a reset with a new 31M genesis.

### 2026-10-15

- Reward split simplified to the v3.2 release schedule: 299/979 of every block to validators, 680/979 to one foundation wallet (`dao_address`). The finance, DAO and satoshi addresses are gone.
- The foundation wallet also holds the genesis allocation; `gengenesis` now writes its address into `param.yaml`.
- `tools/make-devnet-pack.sh` builds a self-contained devnet archive with prebuilt Linux and macOS binaries for launching on another machine.
- Linux: the pack was launched in a Debian container.

### 2026-10-12

- Renamed the project to Zephyrium and the coin to ZEP. The Go module is `github.com/zephyrium/zephyrium-chain`.
- Devnet scripts read validator keys from the uncommitted secrets file; the highway creates its own network identity on start.
- Removed inherited scripts and files that carried upstream test keys.

### 2026-10-11

- ZEP minting schedule: 1,000,000,000 hard cap, 21,000,000 at genesis, 979,000,000 minted by blocks over 21 years with a 10% yearly decrease.
- Every block reward is split 309/330/330/10 (of 979) between validators, finance, DAO and satoshi addresses.
- The minting cap is counted on-chain from the first block.
- Genesis coins go to a newly generated treasury key (`utility/gengenesis`).
- Stake amounts come from config: 21,000 ZEP per shard validator, 210,000 ZEP beacon minimum.
- Devnet shard committee opened to 7 seats with 5 fixed; beacon committee closed at 4.
- Highway bundled under `./highway`. Fixed: staked validators could not report their supported features, so they were never seated.
- Added `tests/devnet/check.py`, a regression check for the local devnet.

### 2026-07-06

- New committee keys generated from fresh randomness (`utility/genzephyriumkeys`), replacing the publicly derivable upstream test keys.
- Working local devnet launch.

## ZEP tokenomics

ZEP has a hard cap of 1,000,000,000. 31,000,000 are pre-minted at genesis for the ICO, and the remaining 969,000,000 are minted block by block over 21 years, with each year minting 10% less than the one before. Every block is split on-chain in three equal parts, the three pillars of the network: validators run the chain, liquidity providers make the markets, the DAO funds growth and R&D. There is no other way to earn ZEP.

:::note On the devnet
The project devnet still runs the previous schedule (71,000,000 at genesis, 929,000,000 minted by blocks, 299 of every 929 ZEP to validators and the rest to one wallet). The schedule on this page is implemented in the chain repository and takes effect when the devnet is reset with a new genesis.
:::

### The schedule in short

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Hard cap | 1,000,000,000 ZEP |
| Pre-minted at genesis | 31,000,000 ZEP (ICO) |
| Minted by blocks on the 21-year curve | 969,000,000 ZEP |
| Yearly decrease | 10% |
| Curve years | 21 |
| Year 1 block reward | 34.478342477 ZEP per shard block (one shard, 10-second blocks) |
| Year 1 minted | 108,805,374 ZEP |
| Cliffs and vesting | None |

### The three pillars

| Share | Of every block | Of the 1B cap | ZEP over 21 years | How it is paid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Validators | 323 / 969 | 32.3% | 323,000,000 | To the beacon and shard committees' reward balances, per seat |
| Liquidity providers | 323 / 969 | 32.3% | 323,000,000 | Minted at the end of each epoch into the SWAP pools, pro rata to the ZEP each pool holds; providers withdraw it with their LP fees |
| DAO | 323 / 969 | 32.3% | 323,000,000 | To the DAO treasury address (`dao_address`) |
| ICO | genesis | 3.1% | 31,000,000 | Pre-minted to the DAO treasury, which distributes it to buyers |

The liquidity part is paid by the pDEX's liquidity-mining mechanism: the chain credits each pool's reward-per-share, and a provider's claim grows with the LP shares they hold. By default pools are weighted by their ZEP reserve; governance can instead set per-pool weights in the pDEX parameters. While no pool holds ZEP there is no provider to pay, and that part goes to the DAO treasury, so nothing minted is lost.

The DAO treasury therefore ends with 354,000,000 ZEP over 21 years: 323,000,000 minted plus the 31,000,000 ICO it distributes. Contributors and the team are paid by the DAO; there is no team allocation, cliff or vesting in the protocol.

### Year by year

All figures are whole ZEP, rounded; year 21 takes the rounding remainder so each column total is exact. Inflation is the year's minting as a share of the supply at the start of that year.

| Year | Total minted | Validators | Liquidity | DAO | ICO | Cumulative supply | Inflation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Genesis | 31,000,000 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 31,000,000 | 31,000,000 |  |
| 1 | 108,805,374 | 36,268,458 | 36,268,458 | 36,268,458 | 0 | 139,805,374 | 350.99% |
| 2 | 97,924,836 | 32,641,612 | 32,641,612 | 32,641,612 | 0 | 237,730,210 | 70.04% |
| 3 | 88,132,353 | 29,377,451 | 29,377,451 | 29,377,451 | 0 | 325,862,563 | 37.07% |
| 4 | 79,319,118 | 26,439,706 | 26,439,706 | 26,439,706 | 0 | 405,181,681 | 24.34% |
| 5 | 71,387,205 | 23,795,735 | 23,795,735 | 23,795,735 | 0 | 476,568,886 | 17.62% |
| 6 | 64,248,486 | 21,416,162 | 21,416,162 | 21,416,162 | 0 | 540,817,372 | 13.48% |
| 7 | 57,823,638 | 19,274,546 | 19,274,546 | 19,274,546 | 0 | 598,641,010 | 10.69% |
| 8 | 52,041,273 | 17,347,091 | 17,347,091 | 17,347,091 | 0 | 650,682,283 | 8.69% |
| 9 | 46,837,146 | 15,612,382 | 15,612,382 | 15,612,382 | 0 | 697,519,429 | 7.20% |
| 10 | 42,153,432 | 14,051,144 | 14,051,144 | 14,051,144 | 0 | 739,672,861 | 6.04% |
| 11 | 37,938,087 | 12,646,029 | 12,646,029 | 12,646,029 | 0 | 777,610,948 | 5.13% |
| 12 | 34,144,278 | 11,381,426 | 11,381,426 | 11,381,426 | 0 | 811,755,226 | 4.39% |
| 13 | 30,729,852 | 10,243,284 | 10,243,284 | 10,243,284 | 0 | 842,485,078 | 3.79% |
| 14 | 27,656,865 | 9,218,955 | 9,218,955 | 9,218,955 | 0 | 870,141,943 | 3.28% |
| 15 | 24,891,180 | 8,297,060 | 8,297,060 | 8,297,060 | 0 | 895,033,123 | 2.86% |
| 16 | 22,402,062 | 7,467,354 | 7,467,354 | 7,467,354 | 0 | 917,435,185 | 2.50% |
| 17 | 20,161,854 | 6,720,618 | 6,720,618 | 6,720,618 | 0 | 937,597,039 | 2.20% |
| 18 | 18,145,671 | 6,048,557 | 6,048,557 | 6,048,557 | 0 | 955,742,710 | 1.94% |
| 19 | 16,331,103 | 5,443,701 | 5,443,701 | 5,443,701 | 0 | 972,073,813 | 1.71% |
| 20 | 14,697,993 | 4,899,331 | 4,899,331 | 4,899,331 | 0 | 986,771,806 | 1.51% |
| 21 | 13,228,194 | 4,409,398 | 4,409,398 | 4,409,398 | 0 | 1,000,000,000 | 1.34% |
| **Total** | 1,000,000,000 | 323,000,000 | 323,000,000 | 323,000,000 | 31,000,000 | | |

Source data: `docs/zep-minting.csv` in the chain repository. The chain-side parameters are `basic_reward`, `max_reward` and the `tokenomics` block of `param.yaml`; see [Network parameters](/validators/network-parameters) and [Validators and rewards](/validators/overview).

## Network parameters

Zephyrium has one network today, the local devnet, configured in `config/local/`.

| Setting | Devnet value | Key in `param.yaml` |
|---|---|---|
| Shards | 1 | `active_shards` |
| Block interval | 10 seconds | `block_time` |
| Epoch length | 50 beacon blocks | `epoch_param.number_of_block_in_epoch` |
| Shard committee | 5 to 7 seats, 5 fixed | `committee_size` |
| Beacon committee | 4 seats, 4 fixed | `committee_size` |
| Shard stake | 21,000 ZEP | `staking_amount_shard` |
| Beacon stake minimum | 210,000 ZEP | `staking_amount_beacon_min` |
| Block reward | 34.478342477 ZEP per shard block | `basic_reward` |
| Yearly decrease | 10%, for 21 years | `tokenomics` |
| Minted by blocks, cap | 969,000,000 ZEP | `max_reward` |
| Reward shares | 323 validators / 323 liquidity providers / 323 DAO | `tokenomics` |
| Genesis allocation | 31,000,000 ZEP (the ICO) to the DAO treasury | `init_tx.json` |
| DAO treasury | Payment address of the treasury key | `dao_address` |

Amounts in the config files are in the smallest unit: 1 ZEP = 1,000,000,000 units.

### Notes

- `basic_reward` is per shard block. A network with more shards or a different block interval needs a different value to mint the same yearly total.
- The committee members at genesis come from `keylist.json`: the first 4 beacon keys and the first 5 keys of shard 0.
- These are consensus settings. Every node must run the same values, and changing genesis or committee settings requires a new chain.

---

## Node types

A wallet talks to a full node. Full nodes pass transactions to shard validators, who put them in blocks. Beacon validators keep the shards in step. Today a highway relays every message between them.

| Node | Stake | What it does | You can run it |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full node | None | Keeps a full copy of every chain and answers queries | Yes, on the devnet |
| Shard validator | 21,000 ZEP | Signs the blocks that carry transactions, tokens and swaps | On the devnet, 2 open seats |
| Beacon validator | 210,000 ZEP minimum | Coordinates the shards and tracks validators | Not yet; the beacon committee is closed |
| Highway | None | Relays messages and serves blocks to syncing nodes | Devnet only; being replaced |

### Full node

It downloads and checks every block and answers JSON-RPC requests. It holds no validator key and never signs blocks.

Run your own for independence and privacy: a wallet shares a viewing key with the node it uses, and on your own node that key stays on your machine.

```bash
./start_node.sh full_node     # RPC on port 9354
```

### Shard validator

A member of a shard committee. Stake exactly 21,000 ZEP, wait as a candidate, get assigned to a shard at random, sync it, then take a seat when one rotates. Seated validators earn a share of every block reward.

A validator must stay online. One that misses too many signatures loses its seat at the end of the epoch.

```bash
./start_node.sh shard0-5      # one of the two spare validator nodes on the devnet
```

### Beacon validator

A member of the beacon committee. Only a key that is already a shard validator can apply. The stake is at least 210,000 ZEP in multiples of 21,000, and auto-restake is always on.

It runs the same program as a shard validator; the beacon staking transaction is what changes its role.

### Highway

A relay server. Nodes do not connect to each other directly today: each one connects to the highway. It creates its own network identity on start and needs no keys to manage.

The [roadmap](/resources/roadmap) replaces it with direct node-to-node networking before any public network.

### What a node needs

Measured on the local devnet, which was nearly idle:

| | Disk growth | Memory at start |
|---|---|---|
| Full node | About 14 GB a year with empty blocks | About 50 MB |
| Validator | About 16 GB a year with empty blocks | About 50 MB |

Transactions add to this. Memory and processor use under real traffic have not been measured yet.

---

## Validators and rewards

The figures are the devnet's settings in `config/local/param.yaml`.

### Becoming a validator

| | Shard validator | Beacon validator |
|---|---|---|
| Stake | Exactly 21,000 ZEP | At least 210,000 ZEP, in multiples of 21,000 |
| Who can apply | Anyone | Only a key that is already a shard validator |
| Auto-restake | Optional | Always on |
| Stake returned | When the validator unstakes or loses its seat | Same |

A staking transaction burns the stake and names the validator key. The validator then moves through four stages:

1. **Candidate**: registered, waiting for the next random assignment.
2. **Syncing**: assigned to a shard, downloading it.
3. **Pending**: synced and waiting for a seat.
4. **Committee**: seated, signing blocks and earning.

Rotation happens once per epoch (50 beacon blocks on the devnet, about 8 minutes). A validator that misses too many signatures loses its seat at the end of the epoch. Today it gets its full stake back; burning part of the stake is on the [roadmap](/resources/roadmap).

### Committees on the devnet

| Committee | Seats | Fixed seats | Open to stakers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Shard 0 | 7 | 5 | 2 |
| Beacon | 4 | 4 | 0 |

Fixed seats are never rotated out. A block is final when more than two thirds of the committee sign it.

### Where rewards come from

Each shard block mints 34.478342477 ZEP (one shard, 10-second blocks). The amount falls 10% each year and stops after 21 years, for a total of 969,000,000 ZEP minted by blocks. Transaction fees are added to the same pool.

### How a reward is split

Every reward is split in three equal parts, the three pillars of the network:

| Share | Part of every reward | Paid to |
|---|---|---|
| Validators | 323 / 969 (33.3%) | Beacon and shard committees |
| Liquidity providers | 323 / 969 (33.3%) | The SWAP pools, in proportion to the ZEP each pool holds |
| DAO | 323 / 969 (33.3%) | `dao_address`, the DAO treasury |

The liquidity share is minted at the end of every epoch into the pDEX (SWAP) pools, by default pro rata to each pool's ZEP reserve or by the per-pool weights governance sets in the pDEX parameters. Inside a pool it accrues per LP share and is withdrawn together with the LP fees. While no pool holds ZEP there is no provider to pay, and that share goes to the DAO treasury, so nothing minted is lost.

The DAO treasury also holds the 31,000,000 ZEP genesis allocation (the ICO). Over 21 years this gives validators 323,000,000 ZEP, liquidity providers 323,000,000 ZEP and the DAO 354,000,000 ZEP (323,000,000 minted plus the ICO it distributes). There are no other allocations, cliffs or vesting; see the [release schedule](/tokenomics/zep).

:::note On the devnet
The project devnet still runs the previous split (299 of every 929 ZEP to validators, the rest to one wallet) until it is reset with the new genesis.
:::

Within the validator share, the beacon committee receives the share of two shards, and each shard's committee splits the rest equally among its seated members. On a one-shard network this gives the beacon committee two thirds of the validator share. Changing that ratio is an open design question.

Rewards accumulate per address and are claimed with a withdraw-reward transaction.

### Checking it

`python3 tests/devnet/check.py` verifies the split after the first epoch (323 to validators, 646 to the DAO treasury while no pool exists), then opens a ZEP/pUSDt pool and verifies that in the next epoch validators, the pool's liquidity provider and the DAO each receive one third. `--stakers` also verifies that an outside validator is seated and paid.
